metadata.description: A CAPM-inspired framework for risk-adjusted molecule valuation. Adapts classical Capital Asset Pricing Model to drug development by defining Rf as the realised all-TA historical approval rate, Rm as the realised TA-specific historical approval rate, and beta as a molecule-level systematic risk estimator. Produces three alpha signals: α₁ (historical), α₂ (pipeline), and Δα (divergence).
citation_sources: Hay M et al. (2014) Clinical development success rates for investigational drugs. Nature Biotechnology 32:40–51
BIO Industry Analysis (2016) Clinical Development Success Rates 2006–2015
Norstella/BIO (2023) Clinical Development Success Rates and Contributing Factors 2011–2020
metadata.disclosure_note: This model and its formulas are proprietary to BioQuill. Two UI modes are available: (1) Methodology tab — full model transparency for institutional users; (2) Simulation tab — apply model to real molecules without exposing formula internals.

framework.overview: Classical CAPM: E(R) = Rf + β(Rm − Rf). In molecule world: Expected PTRS = Rf + β(Rm_TA − Rf). Alpha measures deviation of actual molecule PTRS from this expectation.
key_adaptations: Returns are defined as cumulative Phase 1 → approval probability (LOA), not financial returns
Rf is the drug development universe floor — all-TA realised LOA over 20+ years — not a truly risk-free asset
Rm is TA-specific historical LOA — the expected return of the 'TA market portfolio'
Beta is estimated from molecule characteristics, not from a price time series
Three alpha signals are produced: historical (α₁), competitive pipeline (α₂), and divergence (Δα)

Rf.label: Risk-Free Rate — Drug Development Universe Baseline
Rf.definition: The realised all-TA Phase 1 → approval rate across the full observable drug development universe. Computed from closed cohorts of molecules that entered Phase 1 and reached a terminal outcome (approval or failure). Represents the minimum baseline expectation for any molecule entering Phase 1, before TA-specific or molecule-specific factors are applied.
Rf.source: BIO/Norstella 20-year central estimate (average of 2003–2011, 2006–2015, 2011–2020 published cohorts)
Rf.update_frequency: Only when a new BIO/Norstella cohort study is published — approximately every 3–5 years
Rf.important_distinction: Rf is NOT computed from the current 14,000-trial pipeline database. The current pipeline contains unresolved, active trials whose outcomes are unknown. Rf must be grounded in realised, closed-cohort historical outcomes only.

Rm_by_TA.label: Market Return by Therapeutic Area — TA-Specific Historical LOA
Rm_by_TA.definition: The realised Phase 1 → approval rate for each therapeutic area, derived from the same closed-cohort BIO/Norstella studies as Rf. Represents the expected return of the 'TA market portfolio' — what a randomly selected molecule from that TA historically delivered. Used as Rm in the CAPM formula for any molecule within that TA.
Rm_by_TA.update_frequency: Same as Rf — only when new cohort study published
Rm_by_TA.oncology_paradox: Oncology is BELOW Rf at 8.6% despite receiving ~52% of all global R&D investment. The most-funded TA delivers below-average historical returns — a structural misallocation driven by commercial upside potential rather than approval probability.

beta.label: Beta — Molecule Systematic Risk Estimator
beta.definition: In classical CAPM, beta measures correlation of an asset's returns with the market portfolio. For molecules, a true statistical beta cannot be computed (no continuous price series exists for most pipeline drugs). BioQuill estimates beta from observable molecule characteristics that determine how closely a molecule tracks its TA's expected outcome trajectory versus exhibiting idiosyncratic variance.
beta.formula: β = Cov(molecule_PTRS_trajectory, TA_PTRS) / Var(TA_PTRS)  [estimated from characteristics below]

interpretation.beta_lt_1: Molecule is less volatile than TA average — outcome more predictable, tracks TA history closely. Lower systematic risk.
interpretation.beta_eq_1: Molecule tracks TA average exactly. Expected return = Rm for that TA.
interpretation.beta_gt_1: Molecule is more volatile than TA average — outcome harder to predict, higher variance. Higher systematic risk.

first_in_class_novel_mechanism.rationale: No regulatory precedent, high outcome variance

academic_institution.rationale: Limited regulatory experience, highest execution variance

Phase 2.rationale: Baseline — most molecules in database at this phase

Phase 3.rationale: Converging on TA outcome — reduced variance

failed_ph2_retrying_ph3.rationale: Against prior signal — very high variance

beta.computation: β = 1.0 + sum(all applicable adjustments). Clamped to range [0.20, 2.50].
beta.note: Beta is labelled 'Estimated β' in all UI displays. It is a characteristic-based approximation, not a statistically derived covariance. Transparency on this distinction is required in all client-facing materials.

CAPM_formula.label: Expected Return Formula

variables.Rm_TA: TA-specific historical LOA from Rm_by_TA table
variables.\u03b2: Estimated from molecule characteristics per beta estimation rules

CAPM_formula.output: Expected PTRS — what this molecule should deliver given its TA and risk profile

example.molecule: Hypothetical Phase 2 Oncology, novel mechanism, small biotech
example.interpretation: Given its TA and high-variance profile, this molecule is expected to deliver 7.79% PTRS

alpha1.label: α₁ — Historical Benchmark Alpha
alpha1.definition: How this molecule compares to 25 years of realised drug development outcomes. Answers: does this molecule have the profile of a winner?
alpha1.formula: α₁ = Actual_PTRS − E(R)  where E(R) uses Rf and Rm from historical BIO/Norstella cohorts
alpha1.benchmark_source: BIO/Norstella closed cohorts 2000–2025. Realised outcomes only — approved and failed molecules.

interpretation.alpha1_gt_0: Molecule outperforms what 25 years of history would predict for its TA and risk profile. Historically strong signal.
interpretation.alpha1_eq_0: Molecule performs exactly as historical precedent predicts.
interpretation.alpha1_lt_0: Molecule underperforms historical expectations. Below the profile of historical winners in its TA.

alpha1.update_frequency: Static between BIO/Norstella cohort publications. Updates every 3–5 years.
alpha1.use_case: Investment thesis anchor. BD due diligence. Licensing valuation baseline.

alpha2.label: α₂ — Competitive Pipeline Alpha
alpha2.definition: How this molecule compares to everything currently in development in its therapeutic area. Answers: does this molecule stand out from today's competition?
alpha2.formula: α₂ = Actual_PTRS − Pipeline_Mean_PTRS(TA)  where Pipeline_Mean_PTRS is computed from the live BioQuill 14,000-trial database for the molecule's TA
alpha2.benchmark_source: BioQuill live pipeline database — 14,000 trials, refreshed with each platform data update

interpretation.alpha2_gt_0: Molecule is above the current competitive average in its TA. Stands out from today's pipeline.
interpretation.alpha2_eq_0: Molecule is exactly average within its current TA pipeline.
interpretation.alpha2_lt_0: Molecule is below the current competitive average. Weaker than typical peers in active development.

alpha2.update_frequency: DYNAMIC — recalculated with every platform data refresh. Changes as new trials enter or exit the pipeline.
alpha2.use_case: Competitive positioning. Portfolio benchmarking. Identifying whitespace vs crowded indications.

delta_alpha.label: Δα — Alpha Divergence
delta_alpha.definition: The difference between Historical Alpha and Competitive Pipeline Alpha. Reveals whether a molecule is leading a strong field or a weak one, and whether the TA has advanced beyond its own historical norms.

delta_gt_0.signal: Molecule beats history but lags current pipeline
delta_gt_0.meaning: The TA has improved — this molecule would have been exceptional historically but is average for today. The field has advanced around it.
delta_gt_0.strategic_implication: Review differentiation strategy. The bar has risen in this TA.

delta_approx_0.signal: Molecule is consistently positioned vs both benchmarks
delta_approx_0.meaning: Most stable and interpretable signal. Molecule is performing in line with both historical precedent and current competition.
delta_approx_0.strategic_implication: Predictable risk profile. Good baseline for standard valuation models.

delta_lt_0.signal: Molecule lags history but leads current pipeline
delta_lt_0.meaning: Molecule is best-in-class today but the TA has historically done better. The current pipeline is weak — this molecule is leading a weak field.
delta_lt_0.strategic_implication: Strong competitive position but temper expectations vs historical approval rates. Window of opportunity if historical rates recover.

delta_alpha.update_frequency: Dynamic — updates with every platform refresh since α₂ is dynamic
delta_alpha.use_case: Strategic timing. Portfolio construction. Identifying TAs where current pipeline quality is above or below historical norms.

worked_examples.delta_alpha: 32.6% − 23.3% = +9.3% → beats history more than it beats pipeline → Oncology pipeline has improved relative to its own history
worked_examples.interpretation: Phase 3 Pfizer asset with strong Ph2 data significantly outperforms both historical and pipeline benchmarks. High conviction.

worked_examples.molecule: Hypothetical — Novel CNS, small biotech, Phase 1
worked_examples.interpretation: Lags current pipeline badly (α₂ very negative) but the pipeline mean is inflated by later-phase molecules. Historically, a Phase 1 Psychiatry molecule with this profile is near its TA floor. Δα is high because the current Psychiatry pipeline skews late-phase. Context-dependent — not necessarily a bad molecule, but a very high-risk early bet in a difficult TA.

methodology_tab.description: Full model transparency — formulas, definitions, citations, beta estimation rules. For institutional users who need to understand and defend the methodology.

simulation_tab.description: Apply model to real molecules from the pipeline database. User picks molecule from dropdown (9,754 unique drugs), model auto-populates TA and phase, user adjusts beta inputs via sliders, platform outputs E(R), α₁, α₂, Δα.
simulation_tab.note: Protects model IP while delivering full analytical value to clients
